title: Real-time MFA-relay phishing kits keep showing up. What's actually working against them for you?
content_md:
A few reports recently describe the same pattern: the phishing page relays your credentials and OTP to the real site live, then keeps the session. Cisco Talos documented an AI-assisted Google kit that syncs auth state over WebSocket ( UAT-11985 ). Malwarebytes profiled BlueKit, a subscription kit that grabs session cookies and device fingerprints ( writeup ). CTM360's InsureTrap report covers a kit aimed at insurance portals that relays OTPs before they expire ( report ). Codes by SMS or authenticator app clearly aren't enough on their own. For those defending customer-facing logins, what has made a real difference: passkeys, device-bound sessions, impossible-travel detection, or fast takedowns of lookalike domains? And what was harder to roll out than you expected? submitted by /u/Extreme
